subject: Channel selection: marketplace vs vendor invoice — procurement controls & co-sell implications
messages:
From: Leah Chen <leah.chen@finlytics.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@finlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Purchase route question — marketplace or vendor invoice?

Hi Vanessa,

Quick background: Finlytics is moving to prototype Redwood for a Q4 pilot. Procurement is asking whether we should route the purchase through AWS Marketplace (SaaS listing) or accept a Redwood vendor invoice (direct). Their main constraints: a standard PO with net-30 terms, support for a PO number on invoice, and a short compliance checklist (SOC2 + limited data residency notes). They also flagged that the finance team prefers Marketplace for credit-card-less purchases but would like to understand co-sell and sales credit implications.

Questions for you:
- From Redwood's side, what are the differences in billing timing, refund/credits, and termination notice if we go Marketplace vs direct invoice?
- Will choosing Marketplace affect co-sell eligibility or the ability for your team to claim partner/field credits?
- Any additional paperwork (e.g., reseller addendum, SaaS listing paperwork) that slows a net-30 PO?

If easier, happy to jump on a 20-min call — procurement is on a tight schedule.

Thanks,
Leah Chen
Head of Procurement, Finlytics
leah.chen@finlytics.com

Attachment: Finlytics-purchase-requirements.pdf (stub)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Purchase route question — marketplace or vendor invoice?

Hi Leah — thanks for the clear summary and the attachment. High-level guidance below; I've CC'd Hannah from Commercial Ops for nuances around co-sell and invoice timing.

Short answer (tradeoffs):
- AWS Marketplace: Fast for customers who need marketplace billing, can be purchased without a Redwood PO pipeline change, and supports monthly billing via AWS. However, marketplace invoices run on AWS billing cycles — refunds/credits route through AWS and marketplace fees (~10-20% depending on program) apply which can change total unit economics.
- Direct vendor invoice (Redwood): Supports net-30 PO, PO numbers on invoice, and direct credit/refund handling with us. Better for negotiated discounts and precise contract terms (MSA + SOW). Co-sell: direct purchase makes it straightforward for our GTM and channel teams to attribute pipeline/bookings; marketplace purchases can still be co-sell eligible but require the listing to be on the marketplace and our partner registration to be in place.

Specifics you asked for:
- Billing timing: Marketplace charges appear on the customer's AWS invoice for the month the subscription is active; refunds are processed by AWS and can take an extra billing cycle. Direct invoices are net-30 from Redwood issue date.
- PO on invoice: Redwood can put a PO number on a vendor invoice. AWS Marketplace invoices won't include a vendor PO on Redwood's side — the PO would be a note in your internal systems tied to the AWS charge.
- Co-sell credits: If you want sales credit and joint GTM activities, direct invoicing + a signed MAP/partner registration is the cleanest path. Marketplace can work (we have co-sell listings) but we need the listing live and to log the opportunity in the partner portal so credits register correctly.
- Compliance docs: SOC2 + basic security questionnaires are the same either path; Marketplace may require an additional listing attestation from us but doesn't change SOC2 delivery.

Recommendation: Because Finlytics wants net-30 PO and visibility on PO numbers, I'd recommend direct vendor invoice for the pilot to keep procurement and finance happy and to make co-sell tracking straightforward. If procurement needs the marketplace for compliance with internal purchasing policy, we can do a marketplace purchase for the first month and then transition to a vendor invoice for the committed period.

Next steps:
1) If vendor invoice is acceptable — I'll loop in Commercial Ops to send a draft quote+MSA and confirm net-30 terms.
2) If you prefer Marketplace — we'll confirm listing availability and provide the AWS Marketplace guide (attached).

I'll follow up after Hannah confirms a couple of partner registration items.

Best,

Subject: Re: Purchase route question — procurement controls & co-sell implications

Vanessa — adding a couple of operational details for Leah's team to consider (copying Ben for finance ops confirmation):

- Marketplace margins/fees: AWS Marketplace takes a cut; that affects how we price offers there. If Finlytics expects to capitalize discount or receive promotional credits, those mechanics differ (we can provide a pre-tax comparison sheet).
- Co-sell registration: For co-sell credit on a marketplace purchase we need: a) the listing to be eligible for co-sell, b) the opportunity recorded in Partner Portal within 30 days, and c) the partner registration to include the AE who sourced the deal. If any of those are missing, crediting becomes manual and slower.
- Billing reconciliation: Marketplace invoices often lack granular token-level usage breakout (unless metering is enabled). For early pilots where cost per invocation matters, direct invoices give better line-item transparency.
- Refunds & termination: Marketplace refunds go through AWS support queues and can add 2–6 weeks to resolution depending on the situation. For pilot agility, vendor invoice + credit on next invoice is faster.

Ben — can you confirm we can add a PO number field on the Redwood invoice and that net-30 terms are fine for pilot-sized contracts? Also attaching a short MAP template for proactive partner registration.

Thanks,
Hannah
Commercial Operations Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Purchase route question — procurement controls & co-sell implications

Leah — following up with a short decision set and attachments so your procurement team can act. I've included the MAP and two short guides.

Summary recommendation (pilot):
- Preferred: Direct vendor invoice (Redwood) for the initial 3-month pilot. Rationale: supports PO + net-30, faster refunds/credits, full line-item usage transparency, and straightforward co-sell attribution for our GTM.
- Alternate: AWS Marketplace for immediate procurement speed if your internal process *requires* marketplace purchases. Note: marketplace may delay refunds/credits and adds a marketplace fee; co-sell crediting needs extra registration steps.

Attached: redwood-pricing-sheet.pdf (formal quote options), aws-marketplace-guide.pdf (operational differences), mutual-action-plan-Finlytics.xlsx (MAP to capture milestones & support commitments).

Action items:
1) If vendor invoice works — confirm PO number + billing contact and I'll send a quote + MSA for signature (I can include the PO number on the invoice).
2) If marketplace required — tell me which cloud account (AWS account ID) and we'll check listing availability; expect an extra 5–7 business days for registration and co-sell enablement.

I'll also ask Ben to draft the vendor invoice template so procurement can validate fields before we issue. Happy to join a call tomorrow to run procurement and legal through the exact mechanics.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting the pilot underway.

Best,
